html:
SMTO-UI-0037 — Give this parameter a name before saving

GUID: f21c7457-75c0-4433-8682-dc67ef5c14d3
Slug: ui-parameter-key-required
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • Every saved parameter needs a name, called its Key, so you and the Agent can find it later. The Key box is empty, so nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Overview tab and type a short, clear name in the Key box, for example production-database. The Key is how you'll refer to this parameter with @ in your messages.
  2. Select Save at the top of the parameter. The Key was the only thing missing, so saving now can store the parameter.
  3. If SMTO then says the name is already in use or not allowed, choose a different name using letters, numbers and dashes. Each parameter needs its own name, and the server checks names when it saves them.

What success looks like

  • The parameter shows "Saved" and appears in the parameter list under the name you typed.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the name you tried.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Parameter Store save validation rejected the record because the Key field is blank after trimming.

What this means

  • Parameter saving finds the key blank after trimming. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Parameter saving finds the key blank after trimming.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the key input rather than substituting a value or display label for it.

How to fix it

  • parameter_editor.js collectParameterPayload() throws ui_parameter_key_required when #parameter-key is empty or whitespace. Enter a key (up to 160 characters); the server normalizes it and may still reject duplicates or unsupported characters on POST/PATCH /api/agent/parameters.
  • Enter a supported Parameter Store key before saving.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate supported key identifies the parameter being saved.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
